question: Which cross-border crypto payment routes between countries actually work today?
answer: None counts yet. Of the 15 cross-border routes the International Crypto Map reviewed (evidence through October 3, 2026), it draws none as a working crypto payment route. 5 had live payments (UAE-China mBridge payment and later Jisr launch, Swift ledger multicontinent tokenized-value payments, ANZ-BHP-Citi Swift-ledger Melbourne-New York payments, DBS-Citi live USD Swift-ledger transactions and UOB-HSBC live HKD Swift-ledger transactions), but each lacks a complete record of who paid whom, the final settlement and the receiver's credit. 2 work every day but move ordinary bank money, not crypto (Indonesia-Japan QR payment linkage and Hong Kong-Mainland China Payment Connect). The other 8 are products, permissions, tests or research with no payment shown.

items.title: UAE-China mBridge payment and later Jisr launch

badge.text: Not counted as a working crypto route

items.text: The China-UAE statement already records an AED 50 million first direct Digital Dirham payment through mBridge by June 2024. The 19 November 2025 event is the later Jisr launch and transaction demonstration, not the first-ever bilateral CBDC payment; neither source completes a recurring end-to-end corridor.
kv: first transaction and later platform launch

exact date, payer, payee and participating institutions for the AED 50 million 2024 payment; funding, foreign-exchange and both CBDC currency legs; beneficiary credit and governing legal-finality record; joined correction and failure procedure; recurring bilateral volume separated from whole-mBridge aggregates

items.title: Ghana-Rwanda licence-passporting pilot

badge.text: Not counted as a working crypto route

items.text: Both jurisdictions now support the framework history: signing in February 2025, a two-plus-two PSP pilot and Rwanda-side confirmation of framework approval in October 2025. Licence passporting can change market access, but it is not evidence that money or a crypto asset moved across the border.
kv: four named pilot firms and their home licences; Letters of No Objection and exact host-country permission outcomes; service, asset, funding, foreign-exchange and interoperability scope; any observed transaction, settlement, beneficiary, exception or recovery chain

badge.text: Not counted as a working crypto route

items.text: The Canadian converter is now normalized and the Hong Kong payout capability is documented, but CPN permits an originating financial institution from elsewhere. The evidence does not establish Canadian origin or one completed end-to-end transaction; no route arc is authorised.

items.title: Switzerland-France Project Jura

badge.text: Not counted as a working crypto route

items.text: Both normalized endpoints establish near-real, real-value experimental transactions that concluded in 2021. The experimental wCBDC tokens were not direct central-bank liabilities; final cash settlement occurred in TARGET2 and SIC. The project did not create a continuing CHF-EUR corridor.
kv: CHF and EUR wholesale CBDC plus tokenised commercial paper

items.title: Hong Kong-Mainland China Payment Connect

badge.text: Not counted as a working crypto route

items.text: Both sides establish a production mainland online-interbank-system to Hong Kong FPS remittance link with reported use. It remains a conventional RMB/HKD account-money comparator, not a crypto, stablecoin or CBDC route.

uncertain: Coverage state describes the state of this research, not a jurisdiction's crypto friendliness, adoption, legality or economic importance.
A route counts only with the whole chain on record: the payer and receiver, the money on both sides, the final settlement, the receiver's credit, and what happens when it fails.
Sources are official records and the companies' own announcements, as the country records list them.

catalog_context.title: Crypto around the world: many licenses, no proven cross-border use
catalog_context.answer: Across 22 jurisdictions, we found no verified cross-border payment route that depends on crypto from end to end. The token layer still settles through ordinary banks and national payment systems.

catalog_context.title: SWIFT's blockchain ledger is moving real money
catalog_context.answer: Banks report live payments moving over SWIFT's shared ledger, and Oracle now offers banks a way to connect their own tokenized-deposit systems. No bank has yet been named as live on the Oracle connection.
